'''''Veronica polita''''', the '''grey field-speedwell''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Plantaginaceae]] (Plantain) family. It is native to Europe, southwestern Asia, North Africa, the Arabian Peninsula and a few nearby countries, and has been introduced to many countries worldwide particularly as a weed of cultivation.<ref name="iNat">{{cite web |title=Fermaugh Species Accounts (Veronica polita) |url=https://fermanagh.bsbi.org/veronica-polita-fr}}</ref>

==Description==
A sprawling, blue-flowered [[annual plant|annual]] [[Veronica (plant)|speedwell]], with somewhat dull green, toothed leaves, broadest at the base. The flowers are smallish (4-8(12) mm diam), usually bold blue (though sometimes with a whitened lowermost part), and grow solitary on stalks emerging from the stem at the leaf stalk, the longest ones not clearly exceeding the leaves; they mature to form a fruit capsule whose two lobes are parallel, clothed with long and short hairs. The lower leaves are non-elongated in appearance, whilst the upper leaves are elongated.<ref name="Sell3">{{cite book |title=Flora of Great Britain and Ireland, vol. 3, p. 472 |author=Peter Sell & Gina Murrell}}</ref>

Similar species include [[Veronica agrestis]] (with fruit lacking short hairs, and leaves fresh green, the lowermost elongated) and [[Veronica persica]] (with flower stalks often much longer than the leaves, and the lobes of the fruit diverging like a 'V').<ref name="Sell3" />

'''Variants''' - P D Sell distinguishes var. polita with flowers 5–8 mm diameter, and var. grandiflora flowers 8–12 mm diam.<ref name="Sell3"/>

==Taxonomy==
''Veronica polita'' was given its scientific name in 1819 by [[Elias Magnus Fries]]. It is classified in the genus [[Veronica (plant)|''Veronica'']] as part of the [[Plantaginaceae]] family. It also has two accepted [[subspecies]].<ref name="POWO">{{Cite POWO |last1=POWO |date=2026 |id=812496-1 |title=''Veronica polita'' Fr. |access-date=30 April 2026}}</ref>

*''Veronica polita'' subsp. ''lilacina'' – Native to Japan, Korea, and the Western Himalayas<ref name="POWO subsp lilacina">{{Cite POWO |last1=POWO |date=2026 |id= |title=''Veronica polita'' subsp. ''lilacina'' (T.Yamaz.) T.Yamaz. |access-date=30 April 2026}}</ref>
*''Veronica polita'' subsp. ''polita'' – Native to Europe, southwestern Asia, and north Africa<ref name="POWO subsp polita">{{Cite POWO |last1=POWO |date=2026 |id=77225425-1 |title=''Veronica polita'' subsp. ''polita'' |access-date=30 April 2026}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
Native to Europe, southwestern Asia, North Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, Korea, and Japan. It is introduced to many countries in the Americas and Asia.<ref name="POWO" />

Its habitat in Europe is cultivated ground.<ref name="FEU">{{cite book |title=Flora Europaea, vol. 3, p. 250 |author=Tutin}}</ref>

Its habitat in Turkey is bare soil in open forests, steppe, cultivated land, roadsides, 0–1800 m.<ref name="FoT">{{cite book |title=Flora of Turkey and the East Aegean Islands, vol. 6, p. 720 |author=Davis}}</ref>

Its habitat in North America is fields, ruderal places, calcareous soils, lawns, 0–600 m.<ref name="FNA">[http://floranorthamerica.org/Veronica_polita Flora of North America]</ref>

==Diseases==
It is susceptible to downy mildew disease caused by the oomycete species ''[[Peronospora agrestis]]''.<ref name=Constantinescu>{{cite journal |last1= Constantinescu |first= O. |title= An annotated list of ''[[Peronospora]]'' names |date= 1991 |journal= Thunbergia |volume= 15}}</ref>
